title: Rivers and lakes worldwide lost water abruptly during the record heat of 2023 and 2024, a Science study finds
tldr: River flow fell about 5.7% and active lake and reservoir storage 9.5% below the 1991–2020 average in 2023–24, the sharpest joint drop in a 35-year record.
byline: EurekAlert (AAAS), Phys.org (TU Wien), Nature World News

title: Satellite radar shows Lagos and Alexandria sinking faster than sea-level projections assume, raising flood risk in 20 African coastal cities
tldr: A Science Advances study maps land motion under 20 African coastal cities and estimates more than 7 million people and about $180 billion in assets at flood risk by 2050.
byline: BBC News, Eurasia Review (Virginia Tech release)

title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
tldr: A fibre-optic cable beside a California fault recorded a magnitude 2 earthquake breaking in two adjacent patches 42 milliseconds apart, not as one smooth circular rupture.
byline: Sangwoo Han, YoungHee Kim, Jaewoo Kim et al. · Rice University; Seoul National University; University of Washington

title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
tldr: Two "lenses" acting on photon number focus a 500-photon microwave state for sensing and then map the signal back near vacuum, giving a 19 dB gain over the standard quantum limit.
byline: Ziyue Hua, Chuanlong Ma, Yilong Zhou et al.

title: Lower central dark matter densities in nearby galaxies than predicted by simulations
tldr: Dynamical models of 136 nearby galaxies find central regions with less dark matter than standard simulations predict, and the affected region grows with galaxy mass.
byline: Yu Lei, Ling Zhu, Meng Yang et al.

title: Peatlands drained since 1800 account for about 2.7% of human-caused warming, and the effect could nearly double by 2100
tldr: An MIT-led study in Nature estimates that draining about 15% of the world's peatlands has caused roughly 2.7% of human-driven warming, with emissions set to continue for centuries.
byline: MIT News, Ars Technica

title: MIT team reports signatures of paraparticles, a third kind of particle statistics, in a lattice of superconducting qubits
tldr: Using 16 superconducting qubits, MIT researchers built excitations that pass three tests for paraparticles, objects that follow neither the boson nor the fermion rulebook.
byline: New Scientist, arXiv

title: A US judge finds a second planned seabed-mining lease sale, off the Northern Mariana Islands, violated the Endangered Species Act
tldr: A federal judge ruled that the wildlife review behind a 16 December seabed-mining lease sale off the Northern Mariana Islands ignored the mining the leases could eventually allow.
byline: BBC, Earthjustice

title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
tldr: River flow and lake and reservoir storage fell together worldwide in 2023 and 2024, the largest drop since 1991, with South America responsible for about 70% of the lost streamflow.
byline: Pedro L. B. Chaffe, Georgia Destouni, Francis H. S. Chiew et al.

title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
tldr: The magnitude 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake of 2025 appears to have started in a rough part of the fault, a kind of zone usually thought to stop giant ruptures, before breaking into a smoother one.
byline: Haipeng Luo, Fengzhou Tan, Zhangfeng Ma et al.

title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
tldr: A plasma process melts cement ingredients and forms clinker in seconds instead of hours, using electricity in place of fossil-fuelled kilns.
byline: Qi Zheng, Haiyan Mao, Chengyao Liang et al.

title: Hera's first close-ups show DART left a stadium-sized crater and a tumbling asteroid surrounded by boulders
tldr: ESA's Hera spacecraft has returned the first close images of Dimorphos, showing that NASA's 2022 DART impact carved a crater nearly as wide as the asteroid and left it tumbling.
byline: CNN, Ars Technica

title: Niobium phosphide wires a few nanometres wide conduct better as they shrink, the opposite of copper
tldr: A Stanford-led study in Nature reports that ribbons of the semimetal niobium phosphide only 5 to 6 nanometres wide become less resistive as they narrow, unlike copper chip wiring.
byline: Tech Xplore (Stanford University release), Nature

title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
tldr: Draining peatlands since 1800 accounts for about 2.7% of today's human-caused warming influence, and the effect could nearly double by 2100 even if no more peatland is drained.
byline: Jevan B. Yu, Etienne Fluet-Chouinard, Susan E. Page et al. · Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; University of Leicester; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology

title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
tldr: Delft physicists coupled two minimal Kitaev chains in a nanowire and observed coherent oscillations of fermion parity, which they describe as the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit.
byline: Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo et al. · Delft University of Technology

title: China launches Shenzhou-24 with a Pakistani astronaut, the first foreigner to fly on a Chinese crewed mission
tldr: Shenzhou-24 carried two Chinese astronauts and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Tiangong space station, the first time a foreign crew member has flown in China's crewed programme.
byline: BBC News, Phys.org (Associated Press)

title: NOAA closes a hurricane season split by El Niño: one Atlantic hurricane, record activity in the eastern Pacific
tldr: NOAA's end-of-season summary counts 10 Atlantic named storms and a single hurricane, against 20 named storms and eight major hurricanes in the eastern Pacific, a contrast it attributes to a very strong El Niño.
byline: Phys.org (NOAA release), iHeart

title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
tldr: A dry, stretchy rubber built entirely from bottlebrush-shaped polymers transmits ultrasound efficiently without any gel and kept a wearable imager working for about nine days.
byline: Shu Wang, Runze Li, Zihan Tang et al. · MIT; Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology; University of Wisconsin at Madison; National University of Singapore; Nanyang Technological University

title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
tldr: An earthquake-cycle model that lets the rock around a fault deform permanently reproduces both small and large earthquakes, and suggests that fault zones can be mechanically very weak.
byline: Peng Zhai, Yihe Huang, Jean-Paul Ampuero · University of Michigan

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
tldr: Pretreating the electrode of a perovskite solar cell so its molecular contact layer bonds at several points gives 27.3% efficiency and 94% retention after 400 cycles between -40 and 85 °C.
byline: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang et al.

title: Euclid finds the most distant quasar yet, a 360-million-solar-mass black hole 630 million years after the Big Bang
tldr: Euclid astronomers confirmed a quasar at redshift 8.13, the first beyond 8, whose slowly feeding 360-million-solar-mass black hole strains models of how early black holes grew.
byline: Euclid Consortium, University of Hamburg, Phys.org

title: Webb's dust map of Cassiopeia A suggests the star's inner layers merged shortly before it exploded
tldr: Webb resolved the chemistry of individual dust clumps in the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant and found signs that burning shells inside the star mixed, possibly hours before the explosion.
byline: NASA, Phys.org

title: NASA asks industry to build a 20-kilowatt fission reactor for the Moon, to be ready for launch by 2030
tldr: NASA issued a request for proposals for Lunar Reactor-1, a 20-kilowatt fission system meant to be launch-ready by 2030 and to run on the Moon for at least five years.
byline: NASA

title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
tldr: Hollow capsules with a single hole use the calm they create inside a turbulent fluid to collect particles of one chosen size and release them on demand.
byline: Matteo Sabato, Sarah Chong, Yaocheng Li et al. · University of Chicago; New York University

title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
tldr: Chemists report a modular reaction that assembles benzene rings carrying six different groups, with the position of each one fixed in advance by the choice of starting materials.
byline: Guillaume Mollaert, Hang-Fei Tu, Jacob R. King et al. · ICIQ

title: COP31 ends without an overall agreement after the EU and island states reject a text that does not name fossil fuels
tldr: The UN climate summit in Antalya closed on Sunday with its main political text unadopted, the first such outcome since 2000, after a dispute over whether to mention fossil fuels.
byline: Phys.org (AFP), Health Policy Watch

title: Robot dives beside the Challenger Deep recover the deepest explosive volcanic deposits ever documented
tldr: Seven remotely operated dives on the Mariana Trench wall found rocks from explosive eruptions at more than 6,000 metres depth, in a zone where young volcanism is not expected.
byline: Frontiers in Earth Science, Phys.org

title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
tldr: Measurements from 21 research cruises and a global chemistry model put atmospheric organic nitrogen falling on the oceans at 12.8 million tonnes a year, about 27% of all nitrogen deposition.
byline: Xu Yu, Yumin Li, Guitao Shi et al. · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; East China Normal University; Ocean University of China; South China University of Technology

title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
tldr: Chips smaller than a grain of rice sit inside test tubes and wirelessly report the temperature of a chemical reaction every half-second.
byline: Sukwoo Lee, Evan A. Weingarten, Michael F. Reynolds et al. · Stanford University; Cornell University; Emory University; OWiC Technologies

title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
tldr: Radio observations of gas swirling at the centre of the most luminous known obscured quasar give the first motion-based mass for a supermassive black hole beyond redshift 2.
byline: Mai Liao, Roberto J. Assef, Chao-Wei Tsai et al.

title: EPFL theory predicts the heating power fusion plasmas need to enter high-confinement mode
tldr: Physicists at EPFL's Swiss Plasma Center have a single theory for the power needed to push tokamak plasmas into high-confinement mode, and say ITER has margin while SPARC is close to its limit.
byline: Phys.org (EPFL release), arXiv (De Lucca et al.)

title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
tldr: In a defect-free superfluid of ultracold atoms, widening a narrow channel first lowers its resistance and then, as the channel turns from one- to two-dimensional, raises it again, with a resistance minimum in between.
byline: Simon Wili, Meng-Zi Huang, Tommaso Bonaccorsi et al.

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
tldr: A flat cloud of ultracold potassium atoms simulates a massive relativistic quantum field in two dimensions of space, showing a tunable mass gap and topological domain walls, a step toward lab tests of early-universe physics.
byline: Yansheng Zhang, Feiyang Wang, Paul H. C. Wong et al.

title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury after an eight-year voyage and prepares to become the second spacecraft ever to orbit it
tldr: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission has arrived at Mercury after more than eight years and is set to fire its thrusters to enter orbit, with science operations due to begin in April.
byline: The Guardian, BBC News

title: The US sells its first deep-sea mining leases, off American Samoa, to a single bidder days after a court faulted the review
tldr: The Interior Department sold two seabed lease areas covering 31.5 million acres off American Samoa for the $6 million minimum, with one company bidding, three days after a judge found the wildlife review unlawful.
byline: gCaptain, Yahoo News (AFP), Nature World News

title: Physicists send a "practically unblockable" message through a brick wall by moving an elevator's counterweight and measuring its gravity
tldr: University of Queensland physicists encoded the word "gravity" in the position of a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight and read it through a wall with a gravimeter, at one bit per minute.
byline: University of Queensland via EurekAlert!, The Guardian

title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
tldr: Using entangled photons and a loophole-free Bell test across a 195-metre network, NIST-led researchers certified that a remote party really sat in a target region, without trusting its hardware.
byline: Gautam A. Kavuri, Yanbao Zhang, Abigail R. Gookin et al. · National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
tldr: On a superconducting quantum processor, Google researchers used contextuality to win cooperative games and solve a structured problem at success rates no classical strategy can reach.
byline: Google Quantum AI and CollaboratorsS. Kumar, E. Rosenberg, A. Grajales Dau et al. · Google Quantum AI

title: Astronomers watch a Sun-like star spiral into a supergiant in Andromeda, with Webb confirming the merger
tldr: A star of about 0.7 solar masses merged with a supergiant seven times the Sun's mass in Andromeda after only seven orbits, and Webb observed the aftermath 47 days after the outburst peaked.
byline: NASA, Phys.org

title: Fiji declares a national disaster and Tonga a state of emergency as El Niño drought deepens
tldr: Fiji's cabinet declared a nationwide natural disaster and Tonga a 27-day state of emergency as El Niño-driven drought cuts water supplies, with effects expected to last until at least mid-2027.
byline: Phys.org (AFP), RNZ, NZ Herald

title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
tldr: Billions of ytterbium ions in a crystal synchronise through a shared microwave field and emit regular pulses at microwave and optical frequencies at once, forming a new kind of frequency comb.
byline: Tian Xie, Rikuto Fukumori, Wai-Keong Mok et al. · California Institute of Technology; Stanford University

title: Unblockable communication with gravity
tldr: Physicists sent the word "Gravity" through a brick wall by moving a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight and reading its pull with a gravimeter, at one bit per minute.
byline: Andrew J. Groszek, Charles W. Woffinden, Michael D. Harvey et al. · University of Queensland

title: Voyager 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
tldr: At 5:16 a.m. Eastern on 18 November, NASA's Voyager 1 passed 25.9 billion kilometres from Earth, the distance light covers in 24 hours, a first for any human-made object.
byline: NASA Science, EarthSky, Popular Science

title: US judge voids the endangered-species review behind the first US deep-sea mining lease sale
tldr: A federal judge in Hawaii ruled that the fisheries service broke the Endangered Species Act by assessing only seabed surveying, not the mining that leases off American Samoa could later allow.
byline: Earthjustice, Courthouse News Service

title: NASA ends science operations of NICER, its neutron-star X-ray telescope on the space station
tldr: NASA has retired NICER, the X-ray telescope on the International Space Station, after engineers concluded that a failed internal motor left it unable to track targets.
byline: NASA

title: Nonlinear cooling and control of a mechanical quantum harmonic oscillator
tldr: Using the natural non-linearity of laser light acting on one trapped ion, physicists cooled its motion directly into Schrödinger's cat states with two to five components.
byline: Matteo Simoni, Ivan Rojkov, Matteo Mazzanti et al.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with high-rate symplectic double codes
tldr: A compact error-correcting code that stores six logical qubits in 30 physical ones now has a fault-tolerant way to prepare its starting states, tested in noise simulations.
byline: Naoyuki Kanomata and Hayato Goto

title: The largest US data centres use about 1.8% of the country's electricity, a first facility-by-facility tally finds
tldr: A study of 403 hyperscale data centres estimates they used 68 to 99 terawatt-hours in a year, about as much as a mid-sized US state, with 54% of it from fossil fuels.
byline: New Scientist, Ars Technica

title: Japan's Hayabusa2 abandons its final asteroid target after engine trouble and will fly past a different one in 2028
tldr: With its ageing main engines malfunctioning repeatedly, JAXA's Hayabusa2 will skip its planned 2031 arrival at asteroid 1998 KY26 and instead attempt a high-speed flyby of the small asteroid 2015 BM510 in April 2028.
byline: Phys.org (AFP), The Japan Times

title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
tldr: Stretching magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene by a fraction of a percent changes its electrical resistance up to about 400 times more strongly than the same strain would in an ordinary metal.
byline: Xuetao Ma, Zhaoyu Liu, Jiaqi Cai et al.

title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
tldr: Sonar images taken every second at a Canadian river delta show underwater landslides peeling the seabed back gradually for up to 100 minutes, not collapsing all at once.
byline: Rebecca G. Englert, Matthieu J. B. Cartigny, Megan L. Baker et al. · Durham University

title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
tldr: A global machine-learning map of about 2.9 million river segments finds that dry climates raise nitrate concentrations in rivers even where there is little farming or urban development.
byline: Kayalvizhi Sadayappan and Li Li · Penn State

title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
tldr: A ring-shaped graphene device lets physicists measure the viscosity of flowing electrons directly, and the result departs from the standard theory of metals.
byline: Yihang Zeng, Haoyu Guo, Olivia M. Ghosh et al.

title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
tldr: Twelve dust grains collected in Earth's stratosphere, traced to the Kuiper Belt, carry the oxygen signature of an isotopically heavy water reservoir that stayed separate from the inner solar system.
byline: Lindsay P. Keller, Christopher J. Snead, Ming-Chang Liu et al. · NASA Johnson Space Center

title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
tldr: Splitting the light inside a microscope into separate regions before detecting it recovers fine detail with about five times fewer photons, without any special illumination.
byline: Li Gong, Aonan Zhang, Madhura Ghosh Dastidar et al.

title: Climate Action Tracker finds the warming outlook has stalled for a fifth year, with current policies heading for 2.7°C
tldr: The Climate Action Tracker's COP31 update projects 2.7°C of warming by 2100 under current policies and says even full delivery of every pledge would permanently overshoot 1.5°C.
byline: Climate Action Tracker, Ars Technica (Inside Climate News), The New York Times

title: Atmospheric O2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
tldr: Three decades of precise air-oxygen measurements show the ocean has absorbed a growing share of fossil carbon since 1990, while the net land sink has not grown, contrary to many models.
byline: Eric J. Morgan, Yuming Jin, Elena Kozlova et al. · Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego

title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
tldr: Webb detects glassy water ice mixed with carbon dioxide across the Beta Pictoris debris disk, a mixture that looks like comet ice formed in interstellar space before the star's planets.
byline: S. K. Betti, C. H. Chen, C. Xie et al. · Space Telescope Science Institute

title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
tldr: A red giant wobbling around an unseen companion of about 2.2 solar masses points to an unusually heavy neutron star in a wide, nearly circular orbit that standard binary models fail to produce.
byline: Xinlin Zhao, Song Wang, Guang-Yao Xiao et al.

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
tldr: An independent imaging method built only on calibration-proof measurements recovers the ring around M87's black hole, 42.2 microarcseconds across, implying a mass of about 6.5 billion Suns.
byline: Samuel Lai, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, O. Ivy Wong et al.

title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
tldr: A newly found 3.95-billion-year-old rock in North China formed from ocean crust buried to mantle depths, suggesting a short-lived subduction event early in Earth's history.
byline: Hangqiang Xie, Chunyan Dong, Pengchuan Li et al.

title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
tldr: Tidal turbine blades made of flexible rubber matched the energy yield of rigid blades with active pitch control while cutting fatigue-causing load swings by up to a third.
byline: Zhehong Zhang, Junchen Tan, Eric-Carin Neba et al.

title: Euclid's first major data release maps more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 likely gravitational lenses
tldr: ESA's Euclid telescope has published its first major data release, covering about 14% of its planned survey, with over 900 million galaxies, 60 million possible quasars and roughly 15,000 probable strong lenses.
byline: The Guardian, ESA Euclid

title: ESA's Hera begins close-up study of the asteroid pair NASA's DART mission hit in 2022
tldr: ESA says its Hera spacecraft is now studying the asteroid Didymos and its moonlet Dimorphos from 25 to 30 kilometres away, starting a "crash site investigation" of the first asteroid deflection test.
byline: Phys.org (Associated Press), ESA

title: The two most notorious "forever chemicals" have fallen by about 30% in England's rivers, but replacements are appearing
tldr: An Environment Agency report finds PFOS and PFOA concentrations in English rivers fell 30% and 29% over a decade, while short-chain substitutes such as trifluoroacetic acid are now widespread.
byline: New Scientist, BBC News

title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
tldr: Physicists created a molecular state of two lithium atoms that stays bound above the energy at which it should fall apart, by making two collision resonances cancel each other's escape routes.
byline: Alexander Guthmann, Louisa Marie Kienesberger, Felix Lang et al.

title: Majorana edge reconstruction and the ν = 5/2 non-Abelian thermal Hall puzzle
tldr: Theorists propose that the edge of the 5/2 quantum Hall state reorganises itself into stripes, which would reconcile a long-running clash between heat-flow experiments and numerical predictions.
byline: Tevž LotričTaige WangMichael P. ZaletelSteven H. SimonS. A. ParameswaranaRudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, Oxford OX1 3PU, United Kingdombhttps://ror.org/01an7q238Department of Physics et al. · Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, University of Oxford; Department of Physics, University of California at Berkeley

title: Gemini and Webb find the oldest compact pair of quasars, two black holes that grew too big too early
tldr: Astronomers found two actively feeding supermassive black holes, 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses, only 18,100 light-years apart just 900 million years after the Big Bang, the oldest compact quasar pair known.
byline: NSF NOIRLab, Phys.org

title: NASA studies show how the LISA observatory could find planets with gravitational waves
tldr: Two papers in The Astrophysical Journal work out how the planned LISA space observatory could detect giant planets orbiting pairs of white dwarfs, and how the Webb telescope could confirm them.
byline: NASA

title: A vanished chemical fingerprint dates the switch to modern-style plate tectonics to 2.5 billion years ago
tldr: Curtin University geologists found that a chemical signature of crust formed about 4 billion years ago appears in rocks worldwide until 2.5 billion years ago, then disappears, marking a shift towards large-scale crustal recycling.
byline: Curtin University, Phys.org

title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
tldr: A 30-micrometre magnet levitated above a superconductor at 4.2 K spins at 2.3 MHz, the fastest magnetically levitated rotor reported, with friction so low it serves as a pressure gauge and a dark-matter probe.
byline: Joel K. Jose, Andrea Marchese, Marion Cromb et al.

title: Photonic entanglement swapping with remote quantum dots
tldr: Physicists entangled two photons that never interacted by combining photon pairs from two separate on-demand quantum dots, reaching a swapping fidelity of 0.71, a step toward quantum repeaters built from deterministic light sources.
byline: Mattia Beccaceci, Giuseppe Ronco, Fabrizio Cienzo et al. · Sapienza Università di Roma; Politecnico di Milano; Johannes Kepler University Linz; University of Würzburg; Paderborn University; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
tldr: Applied to 106 X-ray-mapped galaxy clusters, Modified Newtonian Dynamics cuts the needed unseen mass 4 to 10 times, leaving a compact residual that could be dark ordinary matter.
byline: Francoise Combesahttps://ror.org/00cpdar66Observatoire de Paris, Laboratoire d’étude de l’Univers et des phénomènes eXtrêmes, Collège de France et al. · Observatoire de Paris; Collège de France; CNRS

title: Chandra finds a black hole or neutron star behind a star's repeating outbursts
tldr: X-ray data show that a massive star that flares every 113 days is being stripped by a hidden black hole or neutron star, the first X-ray detection of this kind of erupting star.
byline: NASA

title: Global CO2 emissions are set to fall slightly in 2026, but mostly because of the Iran war's oil shock
tldr: The Global Carbon Budget projects fossil CO2 emissions down 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes in 2026, which its authors attribute largely to the oil shock from the Iran war rather than climate policy.
byline: New Scientist, Phys.org

title: Physicists image "ultraquantum" turbulence in a cloud of ultracold atoms
tldr: A Cambridge team directly imaged tangled vortex lines in a turbulent quantum gas, and found it relaxes much like denser liquid helium does.
byline: New Scientist, Physical Review Letters

title: Scaling up chemical recycling: High-yield polyolefin pyrolysis to liquid hydrocarbons using iron single atom catalysts
tldr: An iron single-atom catalyst converts 97% of polyolefin plastic to liquid hydrocarbons with 94% yield, and works at kilogram scale.
byline: Guo-Ping Lu, Xueping Zhang, Kai Xu et al.

title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
tldr: Simulations suggest ocean iron fertilization removes carbon most durably in the Southern Ocean, but only about 30 petagrams of carbon over a century, less than earlier estimates.
byline: Kyung-Min Noh, Xiao Liu, Charles Stock et al.

title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
tldr: An 800,000-year reconstruction of a deep North Atlantic current finds it flips between weak glacial and strong interglacial modes, with abrupt collapses and slower recoveries.
byline: Nathan Stevenard, Aline Govin, Catherine Kissel et al.

title: NASA commits to PROMISE, a nuclear-powered rover built from Mars spares, for the Moon's south pole
tldr: NASA is building PROMISE, a six-wheeled, nuclear-powered rover assembled partly from Curiosity and Perseverance spare parts, to scout ice and resources near the Moon's south pole, with a launch targeted for late 2028.
byline: NASA, ScienceDaily

title: Berkeley Earth says 2026 is very likely the hottest year on record as COP31 opens
tldr: Berkeley Earth is 95% confident 2026 will beat 2024's record, while the WMO's more cautious update puts it among the four warmest years, with a strengthening El Niño pushing 2027 higher.
byline: BBC News, World Meteorological Organization

title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
tldr: Asian cave records show ice-age abrupt warmings took over a century, far slower than Greenland ice cores imply, because Greenland captured a fast atmospheric change, not the ocean's pace.
byline: Xiyu Dong, Xu Zhang, Yuchen Sun et al.

title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
tldr: Stamping honeycomb chips from nitinol sheets and stacking them yields a cooling structure that survived more than 100 million cycles and delivers 3850 watts per kilogram, at about a tenth of the usual fabrication cost.
byline: Changfeng Su, Yang Li, Zhongzheng Deng et al.

title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
tldr: Fourteen years of seafloor measurements show the fault that produced Japan's 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake has already returned to a locked state similar to before the quake.
byline: Fumiaki Tomita, Tianhaozhe Sun, Motoyuki Kido et al.

title: China's space station cools a cloud of atoms to a record 9.7 picokelvin
tldr: Researchers aboard China's Tiangong station cooled about 20,000 rubidium atoms to an equivalent 9.7 picokelvin, about four times below the previous record, and watched the cloud expand for seven seconds.
byline: Phys.org, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: The Arctic polar vortex is breaking down weeks earlier than ever observed
tldr: Meteorologists say the stratospheric polar vortex is weakening in early November, the earliest disruption on record, but the cause and any effect on winter weather remain uncertain.
byline: BBC Weather, Phys.org (AFP)

title: Mantle currents may have helped carve the Great Unconformity, geologists' biggest gap in the rock record
tldr: Simulations of mantle convection over the past billion years suggest slow uplift of continents, followed by glacial scouring, helped create the Great Unconformity.
byline: Phys.org (University of Wollongong), Ars Technica

title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
tldr: A three-way feedback between drying soils, high-pressure systems and heat appears to make the most extreme midlatitude heat waves about 10% hotter, and warming makes the trigger threshold easier to cross.
byline: Yinglin Tian, Jiangong Liu, Yu Huang et al. · Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research; International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis; Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology

title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
tldr: Shot-noise measurements in a bismuth-based cuprate suggest the pseudogap energy equals the energy at which electrons begin pairing, tying a mysterious phase to superconductivity's building block.
byline: Jiasen Niu, Maialen Ortego Larrazabal, Thomas Gozlinski et al. · Utrecht University; Leiden University; Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich

title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
tldr: Researchers built the first tunable three-component Hubbard system from ultracold atoms and imaged it atom by atom, observing a Mott insulator and competing magnetic correlations.
byline: Jirayu Mongkolkiattichai, Liyu Liu, Sohail Dasgupta et al. · University of Hamburg; Rice University

title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
tldr: Models of slow mantle flow suggest continents rose for hundreds of millions of years and then sank, which would erase and then bury the rock record behind the Great Unconformity.
byline: Santosh Dhungana, Nicolas Flament

title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
tldr: A physics-based model of Webb's camera, tuned with the gradient descent used to train neural networks, cuts noise in exoplanet images and revealed a planet that had gone unseen at one wavelength.
byline: Rodrigo Ferrer-Chavez, Jason J. Wang, Katherine L. Bouman et al.

title: NASA's Swift gamma-ray observatory ends its 22-year mission with a fiery re-entry
tldr: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which tracked more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts, was predicted to fall out of orbit on 4 November after a failed rescue attempt, and NASA now lists it as having re-entered.
byline: The Guardian, NASA

title: A hidden companion star may be stirring Betelgeuse's atmosphere
tldr: Radio observations from the VLA and ALMA suggest a close companion star, Siwarha, distorts the atmosphere of the red supergiant Betelgeuse, which has otherwise recovered from its Great Dimming.
byline: ScienceDaily (ALMA release), The Astronomical Journal

title: Uranium cubes show Germany's last wartime reactor was far short of what it needed
tldr: A PNAS Nexus analysis of surviving uranium cubes and archives finds the B8 reactor would have needed 1,292 to 1,775 cubes, far more than the 664 used, contradicting Heisenberg's claim that it was nearly critical.
byline: Ars Technica, PNAS Nexus

title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
tldr: Cryogenic atom probe tomography with deuterium tracers gives the first direct observation of hydrogen dissolved in the gaps between metal atoms, and shows the metal's makeup decides where it sits.
byline: Chao Huang, Saiyu Liu, Wenting Lv et al. · University of Sydney

title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
tldr: Seasonal hydrogen chloride spikes above fresh fissures on Mars's Alba Mons suggest gas seeping from hot magma, a possible sign that Mars is dormant rather than dead.
byline: Alexander Trokhimovskiy, Daniel Mège, Oleg Korablev et al. · Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
tldr: Evidence of chirality in manganese telluride supports altermagnetism as a real third class of magnetism that sits between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets.
byline: Daniel Jost, Resham Babu Regmi, Eder G. Lomeli et al. · SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory

title: Chemical traces of blood found in a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone
tldr: A team led by Curtin University reports red blood cell-like structures and heme molecules inside the leg bone of a 115-million-year-old Brazilian dinosaur, the first chemical evidence of blood in a dinosaur.
byline: Phys.org, The Conversation, Popular Science

title: LHCb sees first evidence of the rarest beauty-particle decay yet observed
tldr: The upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN reports 3.2-sigma evidence for a beauty-particle decay into two muons that occurs about once per ten billion decays, consistent with the Standard Model.
byline: BBC, University of Cambridge, Phys.org

title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
tldr: In a 90-patient phase 2 trial, ivonescimab plus chemotherapy before and after surgery gave a 70.1% major pathological response in resectable lung cancer.
byline: Xiaoliang Zhao, Bin Zhang, Chenguang Li et al. · Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University

title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
tldr: AutoDNA, an AI-run laboratory, coordinates over 20 instruments across more than 11,000 steps to carry out DNA synthesis, amplification and sequencing with minimal human intervention.
byline: Mingyu Wu, Zhaoguo Wang, Jiabin Wang et al.

title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
tldr: Copper complexes of heteroaryl sulfones split apart when hit by visible light, releasing carbon radicals that enable fluoroalkylation of arenes and alkynes.
byline: Zhiqiang Wei, Xiang Li, Lin Xiao et al. · Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, ShanghaiTech University
